2019_140_091719regmtg.paragraph: Agenda and full board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of September 17, 2019, held at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. Contents include recognitions, the August 20, 2019 minutes, the July 2019 Treasurer's Report, probationary contracts for new teachers, a summer professional learning report, and September enrollment counts. The most consequential business is a linked pair of actions: authorization to purchase 1522 E. Big Beaver Road from BTG Big Beaver LLC for a price not to exceed $4,000,000.00, and a resolution authorizing 2019 School Building and Site Bonds (Limited Tax General Obligation) in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed $6,100,000 to pay for the acquisition, renovation and issuance costs.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, September 17, 2019, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions**
- Michigan American Red Cross certificate presented by Leonard Rezmierski and Kelly DeLong; Troy High senior Ian Watson assisted the programs.
- Spring 2019 all-state athletes recognized by Mr. Fulcher: Jenna Doyle, Lauren Fulcher, Cameron Graziosi, Grace Johnson (track and field); Alexis Morse, Sahaja Pinnu, Agata Szewczuk (girls tennis); Jordyn Rauser, Brooke Russell, Tahra Brodbine (girls soccer); Morgan MacDonald (girls lacrosse).
- ASBO International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the CAFR for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2018, credited to Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services.
- Student representatives introduced: Noah Germilhac (Troy College & Career), Pranay Gupta (International Academy East), Noah Scudder (Athens), Amanda Kovacs (Troy High).

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the August 20, 2019 special workshop, regular meeting and closed session, plus the July 2019 Treasurer's Report. August actions carried 6-0 with Mrs. Hammond absent: resolution 19-075 extended Superintendent Machesky's contract from July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2024; 19-076 extended contracts for Rick West, Kris Griffor and Jordan Harris; 19-077 moved the January 14, 2020 meeting to January 21, 2020.

**Personnel and curriculum**
Probationary contracts for 2019-2020 teachers were recommended; Assistant Superintendent Jordan Harris reported 34 new TSD teachers, 2 TSD graduates, 14 with education beyond a bachelor's degree, 6 with five or more years of prior experience (1 with ten or more) and 73 total years of prior teaching experience. The Department of Teaching & Learning reported on 2019 summer professional learning under the "World Class by 2020" vision. Enrollment on September 12, 2019 totaled 13002 students against 13020 on September 12, 2018.

**Business**
A resolution authorized purchase of 1522 E. Big Beaver Road (Sidwell No. 20-26-200-055) from BTG Big Beaver LLC for not more than $4,000,000.00, and a companion resolution authorized 2019 School Building and Site Bonds (Limited Tax General Obligation) of not more than $6,100,000, with Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. as bond counsel and PFM Financial Advisors LLC as financial advisor.

**Other**
Gary Hauff, Nancy Philippart, Karl Schmidt and Nicole Wilson were certified as delegates to the MASB 2019 Delegate Assembly, November 8-11, 2019. Dr. Machesky presented the oneTROY Welcome Back video from the August 20 staff event at Athens High School.
2019_140_091719regmtg.verbose:
Complete agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education held September 17, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. District administration is at 4400 Livernois, telephone 248.823.4000; meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

RECOGNITION. Mr. Leonard Rezmierski, Michigan American Red Cross Board Member, and Mrs. Kelly DeLong, Michigan American Red Cross Donor Recruitment Representative, presented a "Certificate of Recognition" for the district's support of Michigan Red Cross programs; Troy High senior Ian Watson was credited with assisting. Spring 2019 all-state athletes recognized by Mr. Fulcher: Jenna Doyle (Senior, Athens HS Track & Field, coach Tom Cook), Lauren Fulcher (Senior, Troy HS Track & Field, Matt Richardson), Cameron Graziosi (Junior, Athens HS Track & Field, Mike Stallsmith), Grace Johnson (Junior, Troy HS Track & Field, Matt Richardson), Alexis Morse and Sahaja Pinnu (Seniors, Troy HS Girls Tennis, Brian Miska), Jordyn Rauser and Brooke Russell (Seniors, Athens HS Girls Soccer, Todd Heugh), Agata Szewczuk (Senior, Athens HS Girls Tennis, Jennifer Yetter), Tahra Brodbine (Senior, Troy HS Girls Soccer, Dan Troccoli) and Morgan MacDonald (Senior, Troy HS Girls Lacrosse, Holly Frederick). The Association of School Business Officials International awarded its Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2018; the certificate is signed by ASBO President Tom Wohlleber, CSRM, and Executive Director David J. Lewis, whose September 12, 2019 letter to Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, notes review-team comments that must be answered in next year's application packet. The ASBO press release (contact Susan Lambert, Ashburn, VA) quotes Director of Recognition Programs Molly Barrie; the program is sponsored by American Fidelity. Student representatives introduced were Noah Germilhac, Troy College and Career High School senior dual-enrolled at Oakland Community College; Pranay Gupta, junior at International Academy East; Noah Scudder, Athens High School senior, President of Athens Student Congress, Head Drum Major of the Red Hawk Marching Band and intern for U.S. Representative Haley Stevens and Michigan State Representative Padma Kuppa; and Amanda Kovacs, Troy High School senior planning to attend Central Michigan University.

CONSENT AGENDA. Items were the August 20, 2019 special workshop, board meeting and closed session minutes plus the July 2019 Treasurer's Report. President Schmidt called the workshop to order at 5:12 p.m. with Fleming, Gottlieb, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson present, Hammond absent, Superintendent Machesky and administrators West, Harris, DiPilato, Birmingham, Griffor and Carrier attending, and three audience members; topics were compensation packages and Niles program relocation; adjourned 6:04 p.m. The regular meeting opened at 6:13 p.m. with four audience members. Resolution 19-074 (Hauff/Fleming) approved the July 16, 2019 minutes, the May/June 2019 Treasurer's Report, IA-East Schools of Choice Section 105C for 9th grade for 2020/2021, and the Oakland County School Boards Association legislative priorities; Yes 6, No 0, Hammond absent. Resolution 19-075 (Philippart/Hauff) extended the Superintendent's contract from July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2024 without tenure. Resolution 19-076 (Wilson/Fleming) extended contracts for Rick West (Business Services), Kris Griffor (Elementary Instruction) and Jordan Harris (Employee Services) through June 2021. Bloomfield Hills Public Schools officials Howard Baron (Treasurer), Jennifer Cook (Trustee) and Lisa Efros (Secretary) addressed International Academy governance, the complaint against the International Academy Joint Steering Committee, and the IA Task Force. Resolution 19-077 (Fleming/Philippart) moved the January 14, 2020 meeting to January 21, 2020. Resolution 19-078 (Philippart/Hauff) authorized closed session under the Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) for attorney-client privilege; roll call yes from Fleming, Gottlieb, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt and Wilson, Hammond absent. Closed session ran 6:46 p.m. to 6:50 p.m.; the meeting adjourned at 7:50 p.m. Minutes signed by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary.

BUSINESS. One resolution authorized purchase from BTG Big Beaver LLC of property commonly known as 1522 E. Big Beaver Road, Troy, Michigan, Sidwell No. 20-26-200-055, for a price not to exceed Four Million and 00/100 ($4,000,000.00) Dollars, with the Superintendent or his designee authorized to negotiate and execute the purchase agreement after consultation with legal counsel; certification signed by Gary Hauff, Secretary. A companion resolution authorized 2019 School Building and Site Bonds (Limited Tax General Obligation) not to exceed Six Million One Hundred Thousand Dollars ($6,100,000) under Section 1351(2) of Act 451, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976, which permits borrowing without an election when outstanding bonded indebtedness is under 5% of state equalized valuation, with notice posted under Section 308 of Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001. Bonds are in $5,000 denominations, maturing May 1 or November 1 with final maturity not later than twenty years from issue, sold at public sale at not less than 99% and not more than 110% of principal, interest not exceeding five percent per annum with no more than a two percent spread; bonds maturing on or after May 1, 2029 are callable on or after May 1, 2028 at par; a one percent good faith deposit is required; first interest payment May 1, 2020; book-entry through The Depository Trust Company in the name of Cede & Co.; designated qualified tax-exempt obligations under Section 265(b)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code. Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. of Detroit is bond counsel; PFM Financial Advisors LLC, 555 Briarwood Circle, Suite 333, Ann Arbor, Michigan 48108, (734) 994-9700, is financial advisor. Sealed bids are received at 4400 Livernois Road and at the Municipal Advisory Council of Michigan, 26211 Central Park Blvd., Suite 508, Southfield, Michigan 48076; fax (248) 823-4013 or (313) 963-0943; electronic bids via Bidcomp/Parity, Anthony Leyden, 1359 Broadway, New York, New York 10018, (212) 849-5021. Bidders must certify they are not an "Iran-Linked Business" under Act 517, Public Acts of Michigan, 2012 (MCL 129.311 et seq.). Continuing disclosure under SEC Rule 15c2-12 begins with the fiscal year ending June 30, 2020. The notice of sale is signed by Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent; Exhibit C's notice of intended borrowing names "2018 School Building and Site Bonds" at the same not-to-exceed amount. Financing Table 2b models a 15-year Series 2019 issue of $6,100,000 with a TIC of 2.40%, dated date November 1, 2019, first payment May 1, 2020, Debt/TV 3.73%, bond term 15 years 6 months, average life 8.94, interest factor 0.21 and existing LT debt of $7,125,000; annual principal runs from $345,000 in fiscal 2021 to $475,000 in fiscal 2035 at 2.400%, with column totals of $10,183,558 existing LT debt, $617,460 November 1 interest, $690,660 May 1 interest, $6,100,000 principal, $7,408,120 Series 2019 debt service and $17,591,678 overall; footnotes cite $139,575,000 of existing UT debt, $7,125,000 of existing LTNQ debt, $4,000,000 of equivalent IFT valuations and DDA/TIFA debt captures of $0 for 2020.

OTHER. A resolution certified Mr. Gary Hauff, Dr. Nancy Philippart, Mr. Karl Schmidt and Dr. Nicole Wilson as delegates to the Michigan Association of School Boards 2019 Delegate Assembly during the MASB Fall Conference, November 8-11, 2019. Dr. Machesky closed with the video created for the oneTROY Welcome Back event held for all TSD staff at Athens High School on August 20.
